{
  "milestones": [
    {
      "id": "m1",
      "title": "multiple predicates for partition",
      "requests": ["R3"],
      "requirement": "I want iterutils.partition to accept an iterable of predicate callables in key and return one bucket per predicate, with each item going to the first matching predicate and a final bucket for items matching none.",
      "observable": "partition([1, 2, 3, 4], [lambda x: x % 2 == 0, lambda x: x > 2]) == ([2, 4], [3], [1]); partition([1, 2, 3, 4], [lambda x: x % 2 == 0]) == ([2, 4], [1, 3]); partition([], [lambda x: True]) == ([], [])",
      "public_names": ["iterutils.partition", "key"],
      "requires": [],
      "why_requires": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "m2",
      "title": "truncated traceback parsing via partition",
      "requests": ["R9"],
      "requirement": "I want ParsedException.from_string to handle truncated tracebacks without raising IndexError, while still parsing complete tracebacks correctly through the updated partition-based line handling.",
      "observable": "exc = ParsedException.from_string('Traceback (most recent call last):\\n  File \"x.py\", line 1, in foo\\n'); isinstance(exc, ParsedException); full = ParsedException.from_string('Traceback (most recent call last):\\n  File \"x.py\", line 1, in foo\\nValueError: bad\\n'); full.exc_type == 'ValueError' and full.exc_msg == 'bad'",
      "public_names": ["ParsedException.from_string"],
      "requires": ["m1"],
      "why_requires": "ParsedException.from_string calls iterutils.partition; the truncated-traceback fix must be compatible with the updated partition API introduced in m1."
    },
    {
      "id": "m3",
      "title": "cache option for remap",
      "requests": ["R4"],
      "requirement": "I want iterutils.remap to accept cache=True so that repeated source objects are mapped to the same result object and cyclic structures can be processed without infinite recursion.",
      "observable": "shared = {'x': 1}; out = remap({'a': shared, 'b': shared}, cache=True); out['a'] is out['b']; root = {}; root['self'] = root; out = remap(root, cache=True); out['self'] is out",
      "public_names": ["iterutils.remap", "cache"],
      "requires": [],
      "why_requires": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "m4",
      "title": "cache option for research",
      "requests": ["R4"],
      "requirement": "I want iterutils.research to accept cache=True and pass it through to remap so searches over shared or cyclic nested data do not recurse forever.",
      "observable": "root = {}; root['self'] = root; result = research(root, query=lambda p, k, v: k == 'self', cache=True); len(result) == 1 and 'self' in result[0]",
      "public_names": ["iterutils.research", "cache"],
      "requires": ["m3"],
      "why_requires": "research calls remap; its cache option must forward to the cache behaviour added to remap in m3."
    }
  ],
  "expected_causes": [
    "partition's multiple-predicate contract may be misread as all-match filters instead of first-match disjoint buckets, or the final unmatched bucket may be omitted.",
    "ParsedException.from_string has many truncated/malformed traceback edge cases, and the fix may regress complete traceback parsing.",
    "remap's cache option may be implemented as per-call memoization only for leaf values, failing to preserve shared object identity or break cycles.",
    "research may not forward cache=True to remap, or may change its existing match-result shape while adding the option.",
    "the dependency from ParsedException.from_string to partition may be broken if partition's return shape or callable-key handling changes."
  ],
  "verifier_plan": "Hidden tests import boltons.iterutils and boltons.tbutils. m1 tests partition with one and multiple predicate callables, asserting tuple buckets including the unmatched bucket. m2 tests ParsedException.from_string on a truncated traceback string for no IndexError and on a complete traceback for exc_type/exc_msg. m3 tests remap(cache=True) with a shared dict to assert result-object identity and with a self-referential dict to assert the cycle is preserved. m4 tests research(cache=True) on a self-referential dict and asserts exactly one match containing the 'self' key/path without RecursionError."
}
